I'm building an SEO content plan for a game-server hosting company (Nxeon). Use WebSearch and WebFetch (load them first via ToolSearch query "select:WebSearch,WebFetch").

For the following games, research the money keywords and long-tail content angles people search when they want to rent/run a game server. Games: Minecraft, Rust, Valheim, CS2 (Counter-Strike 2), Palworld, ARK (Survival Evolved + Survival Ascended), Satisfactory, Terraria, Project Zomboid, 7 Days to Die, Enshrouded, V Rising, Factorio, Garry's Mod, DayZ, Conan Exiles, Unturned, The Forest, Sons of the Forest, and Call of Duty (via Plutonium: CoD4, World at War, Black Ops 1/2/3, MW2, MW3).

Deliver two things:

1. MONEY KEYWORDS — for each game, list the high-intent commercial keyword patterns people actually search, e.g. "X server hosting", "cheap X server hosting", "X server hosting with mods", "rent X server", "best X server hosting", "X dedicated server hosting". Note which have high volume/competition vs long-tail. Use WebSearch to sanity-check real search phrasing and any autocomplete-style variants you can find.

2. BLOG / CONTENT ANGLES — the informational long-tail topics that pull traffic and funnel to server rentals, e.g. "best X mods", "how to make an X server", "best X plugins", "how to add mods to an X server", version/update setup guides, "best X server settings", multiplayer setup, admin commands lists, "how many players can an X server hold", server requirements.

Then produce a PRIORITIZED list of ~35-40 specific blog post titles across all these games that would realistically rank and drive long-tail traffic to game-server hosting pages. Prioritize by a rough sense of search demand and buyer intent. Group or tag each with the game and the intent (setup guide / mods list / plugins / comparison / troubleshooting).

Be concrete and itemized with source URLs where you validated something. Return everything as your final message text (do NOT write files).
